summary: Generation complete: 88 attempts, 83 billed requests and 5 unbilled connection failures. 31 valid GLB exports; art approval is separate. Props and stylized goats/trees are usable candidates. Polished character reference quality and a full cohesive kit remain unproven.

costNotes.title: What the unit costs include
costNotes.text: Chain costs include every attempt for that model and brief, including failures and model-assisted corrections. Repeat costs include all failed first attempts. They exclude the separately disclosed shared harness and orchestration effort.

costNotes.title: Cleanup is not free
costNotes.text: No human artist performed cleanup. Human finishing time is unmeasured. At $25 / $50 / $100 per hour, 10 minutes per asset adds $4.17 / $8.33 / $16.67. For ten assets, that adds $41.67 / $83.33 / $166.67. Thirty minutes triples those figures. Gateway totals are not all-in production quotes.

costNotes.title: Scene labor scenario
costNotes.text: For the 25-subject Ranch inventory, an assumed 10 minutes of finishing per subject is 4.17 hours: $104.17 / $208.33 / $416.67 at $25 / $50 / $100 per hour. Generator integration, collision/interaction setup, animation binding and QA remain unmeasured and additional. This scenario is not an estimate of actual artist time.

costNotes.title: Adaptive workflow, small sample
costNotes.text: The initial trough pilot used high reasoning/12000 tokens; other initial briefs used high/24000. Later repairs and independent repeats used low/24000 and streaming. This is a workflow study, not an identical-compute model ranking. Only two models received three independent easy-asset repeats.

costNotes.title: Harness work and failed builds
costNotes.text: All 128 Blender invocations were profiled, including 60 failures. Recorded machine wall time totals 472.8s across setup, builds, rebuilds and inspections; this is not human labor. Scene export, root-ground allowance and hidden importer helpers required harness corrections. Original evidence is preserved. A Sonnet foreman correction prompted by the helper bug cost $0.064958 and remains included.

costNotes.title: Production limitations
costNotes.text: All 31 valid exports are registered in the existing asset database. Accepted means reusable candidate approval at current game-scale art quality; it does not bind a replacement into Sandbox. Character prototypes use up to 136 mesh objects, so draw-call batching and scene-scale performance still need work. Polished kit variants were not advanced from an unapproved base.

costNotes.title: Payment and reconciliation
costNotes.text: One $20 credit purchase cost $22.19: $0.88 processing fee and $1.31 tax. Auto-reload remained off. Dedicated-key usage reconciles to $12.1067906 for 83 served requests; 5 connection failures have no recorded charge. Remaining team balance is reported separately because it also includes prior/unrelated activity. Model token usage and failed calls are counted; orchestration subscription usage, electricity and hardware depreciation are not metered here. Existing Vercel hosting/build usage is not attributed to this task; those costs are not included in the Gateway-only figures.

protocol.method: Identical brief and reference inputs. Gateway writes Blender Python. Frozen common harness validates, exports, reimports and renders. No orchestrator-authored geometry repairs. Fixed provider per model; no model fallbacks or automatic retries.
protocol.acceptance: Technical validity AND visual/art review AND required runtime behavior. GLB export alone is not acceptance. Failures remain in denominator and cost. Accepted outputs require existing asset database registration before game integration.
protocol.accounting: Actual Gateway generation cost including reasoning, failures and repair calls. Unresolved requests retain worst-case reservation. Cash top-ups/fees/tax shown separately from consumed credits. Local machine wall time is not human labor. Human cleanup minutes are separate; dollar scenarios at 25/50/100 per hour. Orchestrator subscription usage not observable, not claimed free or included in Gateway spend.
protocol.scope: Production asset-making benchmark; not a promise to recreate all ranch assets for $50. Scene estimate will use frozen production inventory and distinguish unique assets, variants, states and placed instances.
protocol.pilotAdjustment: All five trough pilot calls used high effort and 12000 maximum completion tokens. Observed Luna used10789 thinking tokens and Gemini11521 and both truncated. Remaining briefs and correction rounds use24000 uniformly. Original calls and charges preserved.
protocol.correctionAdjustment: Starting after repair-jobs-2 was launched, further correction requests use low reasoning with the same 24000-token cap, for all models. Several high-effort responses consumed the allowance before producing complete code. Existing high-effort attempts remain billed and visible. New requests stream to preserve generation IDs and avoid long silent connections. This is an adaptive workflow benchmark, not a ranking from identical compute.

sceneProjection.warning: This is an illustrative 24-subject prototype inference subtotal plus an unpriced garden, NOT the cost of an accepted complete scene. Repeated placements are free reuse; new state modeling, untested species, character finishing, scene integration and QA are additional. The general shelter is excluded because the Ranch core uses its six specific buildings.

recommendation: Use Sol as the default for constructed assets; Luna can be useful for simple props with explicit validation and repair. Astra did not justify its higher cost in this sample. Do not promise reference-quality characters from this workflow yet.
